subject: Animation
title: Outsourcing: Animation's Hidden Workforce
description: A fast breakdown of Outsourcing: Animation's Hidden Workforce for builders.

hook.text: Most American animated shows are drawn, inked, and colored by artists in South Korea, India, or the Philippines.

buildup.text: American studios design characters and storyboard scenes, then send the actual animation work overseas.

discovery.text: Outsourcing cuts production costs by 50 to 70 percent, making the volume of modern TV animation possible.

twist.text: The artists doing the work are often paid a fraction of what their American counterparts earn for the same skill.

climax.text: Global outsourcing makes animation affordable but raises serious questions about labor fairness and credit.

punchline.text: Cheap animation has a hidden cost: the artists who make it.

quiz.question: What ethical concern does animation outsourcing raise?
options: Outsourced animation is always low quality
Overseas artists doing the same work are paid a fraction of American rates, raising labor fairness questions
Outsourcing leads to more animation jobs in America

details.summary: A hidden global workforce in South Korea, the Philippines, India, and Vietnam animates much of the world's TV and streaming content. This outsourcing model keeps costs down but raises questions about credit, labor conditions, and creative ownership.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding animation outsourcing reveals the true global nature of the industry. The shows audiences associate with American studios are often animated by thousands of artists halfway around the world.
takeaways: Most Western animated TV is produced by outsourced international studios
South Korea, Philippines, India, and Vietnam are major outsourcing hubs
Outsourcing enables affordable production but raises labor and credit concerns

faq.question: Why is animation outsourced to other countries?
faq.answer: Animation is labor-intensive and expensive. Studios in South Korea, the Philippines, and India offer skilled animators at lower costs. A show designed and storyboarded in Los Angeles is often animated frame by frame in Seoul or Manila.

faq.question: What are the ethical concerns with animation outsourcing?
faq.answer: Outsourced animators often work long hours for low wages and receive no screen credit. The creative contribution of international studios is rarely acknowledged. As these countries develop original content, the power dynamic is slowly shifting.
